name: Melzar
overview: Melzar, described as the steward set over Daniel and his three Hebrew companions by the prince of the eunuchs, plays a crucial role in the narrative of Daniel 1. He is entrusted with overseeing their diet and well-being, as Daniel requests permission for a ten-day trial of eating only pulse and drinking water instead of the king's rich food. Melzar consents to this test, and after ten days, the Hebrew youths appear healthier than those who ate the king's food, leading Melzar to remove the royal food and provide them with pulse. This account highlights Melzar's administrative responsibility and his cooperation in allowing God's providential care for Daniel and his friends to be demonstrated.
